processing: A flat, pan-fired green tea, pressed straight in the pan into a smooth, sword-like shape, as with other flat Jiangsu and Zhejiang greens.
harvest_season: Spring. The one-bud, one-leaf picking known locally as qiqiang is its background; exact dates are not well recorded.
appearance_dry: Flat, straight and smooth like a sword blade, glossy green.
taste_profile: High, clean aroma with a tender freshness and a fresh, mellow cup.

brewing.notes: General advice for flat green teas: keep the water cool and do not leave the leaf sitting.

vintage_note: Sold as the current year's spring green tea, as is usual for its class, and best drunk within the year.
description:
Maoshan Qingfeng is a flat green tea from Maolu town in Jintan, on the Jiangsu side of the Mao Mountains. The name means something like the green peak, and you will also see it written with a different second character meaning green blade, which fits the shape equally well.

The leaf is flat, straight and smooth, like a small sword, with a glossy green colour. Pan work creates that shape, as it does with other teas of this family.

The aroma is high and clean, with a tender freshness, and the cup is fresh and mellow. Water around 80 degrees suits it.

It is mostly a regional tea, so a good seller should be able to say where in Jintan it was grown and in which spring. It makes a natural comparison with Jintan Queshe from the same district.
history: Maoshan Qingfeng began production at Maolu in the 1940s under the name qiqiang, after the one-bud, one-leaf picking. It received its present name in 1983. Little else is documented about the people behind it.
